subject: Mendrix pilot — traffic simulation & temporary rate exception request
content:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Product Team <product@redwood.ai>, Infrastructure <infra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Mendrix pilot — traffic simulation & temporary rate exception request

Team,

Mendrix (pilot customer, DEAL-7842) has finalized their pilot start window: 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-18. They expect a concentrated ramp for two hours/day during the morning peak (US PST) and are asking for a temporary increase in per-minute rate limits for that window.

Attached: mendrix_traffic_sim_v2.csv — this contains our Monte Carlo traffic simulation (1000 runs) and the 95th/99th percentile token QPS per minute. Summary: median burst = 420 TPS, 95th = 820 TPS, 99th = 1,200 TPS for the peak 120 minute window. Their current assigned quota would throttle them heavily at 250 TPS.

Asking for:
- Product: confirm if a per-customer temporary rate bump (policy-based, time-limited) is okay and what guardrails we should require (max 1.5x billing multiplier, canary ramp minutes).
- Infra: feasibility of enabling a routing override to our dedicated pool for Mendrix for the two-hour windows (even if capacity needs a short-lived burst). Estimate of any pre-warm or capacity pinning lead time?
- CS (Marissa): confirm we have the signed amendment (I have a doc link) and whether Mendrix will accept automatic fallback to the hosted model if Dedicated becomes saturated.

Next steps suggested:
1) Infra run a quick preflight: can we absorb 1,200 TPS for 2h on 11/10 without impacting SLAs for other tenants? If not, provide mitigation options (routing to dedicated, temporary soft-quota, graceful 429 policy).
2) Product define exact exception entry (duration, multiplier, billing flag).
3) Sales/CS finalize payment security and amendment text.

I will forward Mendrix's ask below.

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

----- Forwarded message -----
From: Alex Moore <alex.moore@mendrix.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 14:05:12 -0800
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Subject: Pilot traffic profile and ask

Jonas —
Appreciate the run-through on Friday. We ran an internal load test and attached our export. For the pilot we plan to simulate our production peak: 150 clients, 3 requests/sec average per client, but spikes when users onboard new datasets — that's where the 1,200 TPS 99th shows up in your sim.

We would like a temporary higher per-minute rate during the pilot mornings (9–11am PST) and will accept a short-term surcharge and a fallback policy to the hosted standard model if dedicated capacity is unavailable. Can Redwood confirm routing and whether we need to sign any addendum?

— Alex
Director, Engineering — Mendrix

-----------------------------

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mendrix pilot — traffic simulation & temporary rate exception request

Jonas —
I've confirmed Mendrix signed the pilot amendment; the DocuSign completes and the HubSpot record are linked below. We also need to ensure billing handles the surcharge cleanly (Karthik, can you own how we surface the temporary multiplier on invoicing?).

For the customer-facing side: they'd prefer automated fallback but want visibility if throttling occurs. So we should expose a short-lived alert to Mendrix Ops and CS if request rejection rate climbs >0.5% during the window.

I can monitor and own communications during the pilot.

Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mendrix pilot — traffic simulation & temporary rate exception request

Quick note: Finance needs a clear flag in the amendment specifying the temporary billing multiplier and which metric triggers it (e.g., peak-avg > 500 TPS for > 5 minutes). I can draft the billing clause but want Product to specify the exact gating condition (Grace?). Also: are we OK with a capped surcharge of up to 1.5x for the exception window?

Karthik
Director, Revenue Operations

-----------------------------

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Product Team <product@redwood.ai>, Infra <infra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mendrix pilot — traffic simulation & temporary rate exception request

Thanks for the sim, Jonas. Short technical readout:
- On current dedicated pools, an immediate 1,200 TPS sustained for 120 minutes will push memory/KV cache pressure up ~35% and token latency up ~18% in the worst-case paths (quantized models).
- Fast mitigations we can do before 11/10: pre-warm routing rules (needs 36–48 hours to shift cold-start profiles), and enable prefix caching for Mendrix prompt templates (we can ship a config change within 8 hours).
- If Product allows temporary routing to a burst node group, we can isolate the load. That requires a short maintenance window to pin the burst group; estimate ~4–6 hours of infra ops prep.

We cannot safely accept unbounded spikes without either: explicit capacity pin or a governed soft-throttle (graceful 429s with retry-after) that CS will communicate. If Product wants a user-visible rollback plan, we can implement automatic fallback to the hosted smaller model but we'd need the customer's sign-off for the change in model quality.

Neha
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

-----------------------------

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Product Team <product@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mendrix pilot — traffic simulation & temporary rate exception request

Thanks — product POV: we can approve a time-limited exception with these constraints:
- Duration: max 2 hours/day for the pilot window (exact days 11/10–11/18 to be listed in the amendment).
- Multiplier cap: 1.5x the signed baseline quota for billing and SLO calculations.
- Safety gates: infra must provide a pre-warm and a soft-throttle policy; we will not allow silent model-downs without explicit customer opt-in.
- Gating condition: exception engages only if observed minute-average > 500 TPS for > 3 consecutive minutes (to avoid flapping on single-minute spikes).

Product will provide the policy doc and the temporary rule set by EOD 2026-11-05. We will also require CS to ack before the first scheduled exception window.

Grace
Sr. Product Manager, Serving

-----------------------------

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Moore <alex.moore@mendrix.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Nov 2026 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Mendrix pilot — traffic simulation & temporary rate exception request

Thanks everyone — summary and action items: 
1) Product (Grace) to publish exception policy doc + machine-readable rule set (will include gating condition: >500 TPS minute-avg for >3 minutes) — due EOD 2026-11-05.
2) Infra (Neha) to pre-warm routing and prepare burst node group; provide go/no-go by 11/09 12:00 PST. Also ship the prefix-caching config within 8 hours.
3) CS (Marissa) to own customer communications and alerting thresholds (0.5% reject alert) and to confirm DocuSign amendment — Marissa confirms signed.
4) Revenue Ops (Karthik) to draft the billing clause for a capped 1.5x surcharge and confirm invoicing flow.
5) Sales (me) to coordinate the first dry-run on 11/09 10:00–10:30 PST with Mendrix Ops and Infra.

Mendrix (Alex) — we will share the final exception terms and a brief runbook before 11/09 dry-run. Please confirm whether the 9–11am PST window is fixed or if you want to shift to 8–10am for earlier warm starts.

Attachments referenced: mendrix_traffic_sim_v2.csv (detailed sim), proposed-sla-exception-terms.pdf (draft clause), routing-matrix-v1.png (proposed routing override).

Jonas
Head of Sales Engineering
